Hi Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the intake: 

Highlights from discovery:
- Primary product use: short-form customer support triage (email -> categorization + recommended responses) and an internal assistant for agents.
- Latency target: median < 250ms for single-turn suggestions on dedicated capacity.
- Data concerns: customer PII in prompts (payment tokens, SSNs), occasional legal citations that must be preserved.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
- Models to try: small to mid 7B quantized variants for latency/cost baseline; 13B float/8-bit for quality-sensitive routes. We can run both in parallel during the eval.
- Benchmarks: we'll run our standard support triage eval (precision/recall, hallucination checks) — link to harness below.

What we need from Voya to get started with a proper model-fit eval:
1) A sample prompt set: 200–500 real user queries (CSV) covering typical, edge, and ambiguous cases. Label columns: id, user_text, expected_label (if available), redaction_tag (if PII present).
2) Edge cases: ~20 examples that historically fail or are sensitive (include why).
3) Redaction guidance: your legal team's list of fields to remove vs. pseudonymize vs. preserve.
4) Access: HubSpot deal id and a shared drive folder for uploads.

Attached: redwood_eval_plan_voya.pdf (outline + timeline).

Next steps / asks:
- Can you upload the CSV and a short PII mapping by EOD Wed (4/19)?
- If you prefer, drop the file in the shared Drive link below and we’ll pull it.
- Proposed follow-up: 30m on Thu 4/20 to review intake and confirm evaluation plan.

Thanks — we’ll treat any sample data as confidential and provide a redaction checklist.

Best,
Ben

Thanks — this is perfect for initial testing. A few follow-ups and clarifications: 

1) Legal citations: please include the full citation string where available. For evaluation we measure whether the model preserves citation integrity (avoid truncation/hallucination). If legal wants to redact later, flag it in redaction_tag.

2) PII mapping looks good. Our guidance (won't change your artifact) is:
   - Remove full payment card numbers and replace with <CARD_TOKEN>.
   - Pseudonymize names to preserve conversational structure when useful (e.g., <CUSTOMER_NAME>).
   - Keep order IDs if they are needed to reproduce routing behavior, but mark as tokenized if they contain embedded user data.

3) Quality/regression concerns: we will run a baseline using two variants (7B-quant and 13B-8bit). We’ll report on: accuracy to label, false-positive rate on policy checks, and hallucination rate (measured via a curated hallucination prompt set). If you have historical failure examples, please mark them — we will prioritize those in the regression suite.

4) Timeline: once we have the 200–500 sample set, we can return an initial eval report within 5 business days.

Links I referenced: https://redwood.ai/evals/benchmark/low-latency (benchmark harness) and I linked the HubSpot deal on our side for tracking.

Would you be able to confirm upload to the Drive by EOD Wed so we can kick off? If not, propose alternate timing.

Also cc'ing Grace who will handle the prompt redaction review and Naomi for evaluation orchestration.

—Ben

Hi Maya — looping in a short redaction checklist to make the intake fast.

Redaction checklist (suggested):
- Remove/replace: full credit card PANs, CVV, full SSNs, OAuth tokens, authentication cookies.
- Pseudonymize: customer names, email addresses, phone numbers with consistent tokens (<CUST_1>, <CUST_2>).
- Preserve: dates and case identifiers where needed for routing/diagnostics (tokenize if they contain personal data).
- Edge-case note: if a prompt contains a quoted legal citation or statute, keep the citation string but mark as "legal_preserve" in redaction_tag.

Upload guidance:
- Filename convention: voya_prompts_YYYYMMDD.csv; include a metadata row with source, time window, and redaction notes.
- If you can't share raw text, please provide an anonymized subset (we can run a separate evaluation for redaction-sensitive cases).

I'll review voya_sample_prompts.csv later today and flag any rows that need additional sanitization. Naomi will take over the evaluation baseline orchestration once the cleaned corpus is available.

Best,
Grace O'Connor | Security & Compliance Liaison, Redwood Inference
